blocks.title: A local, family-run school built on passion.
body: Welcome to Mauritius! Born To Kite is a local, family-run school founded in January 2026. I have taught kitesurfing for more than ten years, and my goal is simple: to share my passion with patience, a friendly atmosphere and the highest possible level of safety.
Escape into the turquoise waters of Mauritius, discover an exciting sport and enjoy an experience shaped around you.
We are based in the south of Mauritius, mainly on Le Morne lagoon. Depending on the weather, we can move to another spot in the area to give you the best possible conditions.

pages.title: Le Morne spot: wind, seasons and safety
pages.description: A guide to Le Morne lagoon: prevailing wind, trade-wind season, flat water protected by the coral reef and right-of-way rules on the water.

blocks.title: A lagoon shaped by volcano and coral.
body: Mauritius was formed by volcanic activity around 8 million years ago. Today, an almost continuous coral reef surrounds the island, creating a shallow lagoon protected from the large Indian Ocean swells and providing an ideal setting for learning to kitesurf safely.

Le Morne, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, owes its dramatic landscape to this volcanic origin. Its peninsula creates a stretch of water that is both windy and sheltered, unlike anywhere else on the island.

Coral reefs are a fragile ecosystem. They support much of Mauritius' marine life and protect the coastline from erosion. When riding, we stay over sandy areas and make sure the equipment never touches the coral.

blocks.alt: Le Morne and its lagoon seen from the air, Mauritius

blocks.title: The wind
body: At Le Morne, the prevailing south-easterly trade wind is generally stronger in the early afternoon. Our instructors check the conditions before every session and choose equipment suited to the wind strength and your level.
Le Morne lagoon is protected by the coral reef. The water is flat and free from large waves, making it an ideal place to learn.

items.title: The wind
items.body: At Le Morne, the prevailing south-easterly trade wind is generally stronger in the early afternoon.

items.title: The waves
items.body: The inside of the lagoon remains flat. Surfable waves are found offshore beyond the reef, with coaching adapted to each person's level.

items.title: Safety
items.body: Being able to swim is better; buoyancy vests are available. Give way to the surfer already riding the wave and keep a safe distance from other water users.

blocks.lead: Conditions observed by the school to help you choose the period best suited to your level. These figures are for kitesurfing: wingfoiling needs fewer knots.

blocks.title: Choosing when to visit.
body: The wind generally blows from 7:00 am to 6:30 pm and is stronger in the early afternoon. It also depends on the tide and increases as the tide rises.
From November to April, the school adapts to the conditions. If there is not enough wind, the session is refunded or rescheduled, or we may move to another spot.
December, January and February are the low season: you can kite, but on fewer days in the month and less regularly.
The lagoon is busier from May to September and starts to become quieter from late September.

items.q: The downwind rider has priority
items.a: The rider who is downwind always has priority.

items.q: Never cross a kite line
items.a: Never pass between a rider and their kite or over their lines.

items.q: Anticipate and communicate
items.a: If in doubt, slow down and give way.

pages.title: Best time to kitesurf in Mauritius, month by month
pages.description: When to kite at Le Morne? June to September for strong wind, March to May and October for a quieter lagoon. Wind, rideable days and water, month by month.

blocks.title: When is the best time to kitesurf in Mauritius?
body: The best time to kitesurf at Le Morne is June to September. The wind then blows at 15 to 33 knots, with 20 to 30 rideable days in August and September. March, April, May and October are still good, with a quieter lagoon. December to February is the low season: you can still kite, but on fewer days and less regularly.

blocks.lead: Conditions observed by the school to help you choose the period best suited to your level. These figures are for kitesurfing: wingfoiling needs fewer knots.

blocks.title: Which month for a beginner?
body: Every month from March to November suits a beginner. The lagoon stays flat, and the kite size is matched to the day's wind. March, April and May bring medium wind, 10 to 22 knots, and fewer people on the water.

blocks.title: Which month for experienced riders?
body: June, July, August and September: the wind is strong, 15 to 33 knots. It is the season for the Bel Ombre → Le Morne downwind and for jump sessions. The lagoon is also busiest from May to September, then empties from late September.

blocks.title: What about November to April?
body: The school stays open and adapts. If there is not enough wind, the session is refunded or rescheduled, and the school may move to another spot for better conditions. December, January and February are the low season: you can kite, but on fewer days in the month and less regularly.

blocks.title: What time does the wind blow?
body: In season, the wind blows from 7:00 am to 6:30 pm. It is stronger in the early afternoon and increases as the tide rises.

blocks.title: What wetsuit do I need?
body: The water stays between 24 and 27 °C all year: a rash vest is enough from November to April, a wetsuit is useful from May to October. Nothing to buy: rash vests, wetsuits and booties are provided by the school.

items.q: Can you kitesurf in Mauritius in December or January?
items.a: Yes, it is the low season: you can kite, but on fewer days in the month and less regularly.

items.q: What about wingfoiling?
items.a: It needs less wind than kitesurfing, so more days are possible.

pages.description: How many hours to ride on your own, what it costs, from what age. Answers from a Le Morne instructor, on a flat lagoon with equipment included.

blocks.title: How long does it take to learn kitesurfing?
body: It usually takes 6 to 10 hours of lessons to ride on your own. At Le Morne, you learn on a shallow, flat lagoon protected by the coral reef. A 6-hour package costs €420 as a private lesson, or €230 per person semi-private.

blocks.alt: Ground briefing before a kitesurf lesson at Le Morne

blocks.title: What happens in the first lesson?
body: No experience is needed. The lesson starts with theory and kite handling on land, before going into the water. You don't need to be able to swim: you can stand everywhere in the lagoon. Being comfortable in the water is a plus.
All equipment is provided: kite, board, harness, helmet, vest, rash vest or wetsuit and booties, matched to your size and the day's wind.

blocks.title: Why learn on Le Morne lagoon?
body: The lagoon is shallow, you can stand everywhere, and the reef protects it from big swells. The water is flat, with no big waves. The prevailing wind is the south-east trade wind, stronger in the early afternoon.

blocks.title: Private or semi-private?
body: In a private lesson, the instructor is with you alone. Semi-private means two students at most per instructor. You can come as a pair, or be matched with another student of the same level.

pages.title: From kitesurf to wingfoil: how many hours to fly?
pages.description: An independent kitesurfer usually gets up on the foil after 4 to 6 hours of wingfoil, versus 6 to 10 hours for a beginner. What changes, and where to learn in Mauritius.

blocks.title: From kitesurf to wingfoil: how long does it take?
body: An independent kitesurfer usually needs 4 to 6 hours to get up on the foil. A complete beginner needs more like 6 to 10 hours. Wingfoiling needs less wind than kitesurfing, so at Le Morne it opens up more days on the water.

blocks.alt: Wingfoiling on Le Morne lagoon, Mauritius

blocks.title: What does kitesurfing give you?
body: You already know how to read the wind, position yourself on the water and follow the right-of-way rules. That is what saves several hours compared with a complete beginner.

blocks.title: What changes?
body: The wing is held in your hands, with no lines or bar. Balance happens on the foil, a board that lifts above the water.

blocks.title: Which lesson should I choose?
body: Wingfoil lessons cost the same as kitesurf lessons: 2 hours for €150 private, or €80 per person semi-private. For 4 to 6 hours, the 6-hour package (€420 private, €230 per person semi-private) fits best.
Once you are independent, supervision costs €30 per hour and rental €20.

items.q: Do kitesurfers learn wingfoil faster?
items.a: Yes: usually 4 to 6 hours, versus 6 to 10 hours for a beginner.

items.q: Do you need a lot of wind for wingfoil?
items.a: Less than for kitesurfing.

items.q: Is equipment included?
items.a: Yes, all equipment is provided, including rash vest, wetsuit and booties.

blocks.title: What is a surf lesson like?
body: A surf lesson lasts 1 h 30 and costs €60, equipment included. The spot is chosen on the day according to the swell, among several spots in the south of the island. Beginners are welcome.

blocks.title: Who is it for?
body: All levels, from your first surf lesson to surfers who want to improve. Being able to swim is better; buoyancy vests are available.

blocks.title: The waves
body: The inside of the lagoon remains flat. Surfable waves are found offshore beyond the reef, with coaching adapted to each person's level.

blocks.title: Safety
body: Being able to swim is better; buoyancy vests are available. Give way to the surfer already riding the wave and keep a safe distance from other water users.

items.q: How much is a surf lesson in Mauritius?
items.a: €60 for 1 h 30, equipment included.

items.q: Where do the surf lessons take place?
items.a: On several spots in the south of the island, chosen on the day according to the swell. Le Morne lagoon stays flat: the waves are beyond the reef.

items.q: Do I need to know how to surf?
items.a: No, beginners are welcome. Being able to swim is better; buoyancy vests are available.

items.q: How do I book?
items.a: On WhatsApp, with your availability. The time is confirmed according to the swell.

pages.description: Meet the team and discover the languages we speak.

blocks.title: A local, family-run school built on passion.
body: Welcome to Mauritius! Born To Kite is a local, family-run school founded in January 2026. I have taught kitesurfing for more than ten years, and my goal is simple: to share my passion with patience, a friendly atmosphere and the highest possible level of safety.
Escape into the turquoise waters of Mauritius, discover an exciting sport and enjoy an experience shaped around you.
We are based in the south of Mauritius, mainly on Le Morne lagoon. Depending on the weather, we can move to another spot in the area to give you the best possible conditions.
